11-1.title: Early Peoples of the Americas
11-1.learn:
KEY IDEAS — EARLY PEOPLES OF THE AMERICAS

Long ago, early peoples settled across North, Central, and South America. Many scientists believe the first peoples reached the Americas thousands of years ago, possibly by crossing a land bridge from Asia during the Ice Age, then spreading out across the two continents.

Like peoples elsewhere, they learned to FARM. The most important crop was MAIZE (corn), along with beans and squash. These three crops are often called the 'Three Sisters' because they grew well together. Farming was a turning point in the Americas just as it was in Africa and Asia: it allowed people to settle down, store surplus food, and grow larger communities.

Over time, farming let some American peoples build villages and then large CITIES and CIVILIZATIONS. The amazing thing is that these cultures grew FAR AWAY from the river valleys of Africa and Asia, with no contact between them, yet they solved many of the SAME challenges — developing farming, cities, government, and writing on their own. This shows that civilization can develop independently in different parts of the world. Remember: maize (corn) was the key crop of the Americas.

questions.question: What was the most important crop for early peoples of the Americas?
questions.explanation: Maize, or corn, was the key crop of the Americas.

questions.question: Besides corn, which two crops did early American peoples grow?
questions.explanation: Corn, beans, and squash were grown together.

questions.question: Many scientists believe the first peoples reached the Americas by doing what?

choices.A: Crossing a land bridge from Asia during the Ice Age

questions.explanation: Many believe early peoples crossed a land bridge from Asia.

questions.question: How did farming change life for early American peoples?

choices.A: It let them settle down and build larger communities
choices.B: It forced them to wander forever
choices.D: It had no effect at all

questions.explanation: Farming allowed settling, surplus food, and larger communities.

questions.question: On which continents did early American peoples settle?
questions.explanation: Early peoples settled across North, Central, and South America.

questions.question: Corn, beans, and squash grown together are often called what?
questions.explanation: Corn, beans, and squash are nicknamed the Three Sisters.

questions.question: What is surprising about how civilizations grew in the Americas?

choices.A: They were taught by the Romans
choices.D: They grew far from Africa and Asia, with no contact, yet solved similar challenges

questions.explanation: American civilizations developed independently yet solved the same problems.

questions.question: What did farming let some American peoples eventually build?
questions.explanation: Farming allowed the growth of villages, cities, and civilizations.

questions.question: What big lesson does the rise of American civilizations teach?

choices.A: Farming was unknown in the Americas
choices.B: All civilizations came from one place
choices.C: Civilization can develop independently in different parts of the world
choices.D: Only river valleys could grow cities

questions.explanation: American civilizations show that civilization can arise independently.

questions.question: Farming was a turning point in the Americas similar to what event in Africa and Asia?
questions.explanation: Like the Agricultural Revolution elsewhere, farming transformed American life.

questions.question: What is another common name for the crop maize?
questions.explanation: Maize is another name for corn.

questions.question: During which period do many scientists believe people first crossed into the Americas?
questions.explanation: The crossing is believed to have happened during the Ice Age.

questions.question: From which continent do many scientists think the first peoples of the Americas came?
questions.explanation: Many believe the first peoples crossed a land bridge from Asia.

questions.question: Why are corn, beans, and squash nicknamed the 'Three Sisters'?

choices.A: They were named after three goddesses
choices.D: They were each shaped like a person

questions.explanation: They earned the nickname because they grew well together.

questions.question: What does it mean that food was stored as a 'surplus'?

choices.A: There was extra food beyond what was needed right away
choices.B: All the food was thrown out
choices.D: Food was traded for gold only

questions.explanation: A surplus means extra food beyond immediate needs.

questions.question: Which sequence shows how communities grew in the Americas after farming began?
questions.explanation: Farming led to villages, then cities, then civilizations.

questions.question: Which of these was NOT one of the Three Sisters crops?
questions.explanation: Wheat was not one of the Three Sisters; the three were corn, beans, and squash.

questions.question: A land bridge is best described as what?

choices.A: A stretch of dry land connecting two areas usually separated by water
choices.B: A wooden bridge built over a river

questions.explanation: A land bridge is dry land connecting areas normally separated by water.

questions.question: A family settles in one place and grows enough corn to feed everyone and have extra. This is an example of what change?

choices.A: Giving up hunting forever and starving
choices.B: Moving farther away every single day
choices.C: Farming allowing people to settle and store surplus food

questions.explanation: This shows farming allowing settlement and stored surplus food.

questions.question: Why is it surprising that American peoples developed cities and government on their own?

choices.A: They had help from Roman teachers
choices.B: They had no contact with Africa or Asia, yet solved the same challenges
choices.C: They lived in the exact same river valleys

questions.explanation: They had no contact with Africa or Asia yet solved the same challenges.

questions.question: Which crop was the KEY crop that supported civilization in the Americas?
questions.explanation: Maize, or corn, was the key crop of the Americas.

questions.question: What direct effect did learning to farm have on early American peoples?

choices.A: They lost the ability to make tools
choices.B: They had to leave the Americas
choices.C: They forgot how to gather food
choices.D: They could stop moving and form permanent settlements

questions.explanation: Farming let them stop moving and form permanent settlements.

questions.question: The civilizations of Africa and Asia first grew up near what landform?
questions.explanation: Those civilizations grew up in river valleys.

questions.question: Which statement BEST describes the early peoples of the Americas?

choices.A: They never learned to farm or build
choices.B: They settled the continents, farmed maize, and built civilizations on their own
choices.C: They were taught everything by Egypt
choices.D: They only lived in South America

questions.explanation: They settled the Americas, farmed maize, and built civilizations on their own.

questions.question: Compared with hunting and gathering, farming gave communities what advantage?

choices.B: No need to live near water
choices.C: A steadier food supply that could feed more people

questions.explanation: Farming gave a steadier food supply that could feed more people.

questions.question: Which group of three crops did early American peoples plant together?
questions.explanation: They planted corn, beans, and squash together.

questions.question: What does the term 'civilization' refer to?

choices.B: An advanced society with cities, government, and culture
choices.C: A group that never settles down

questions.explanation: A civilization is an advanced society with cities, government, and culture.

questions.question: Because American civilizations grew with no contact with the Old World, historians conclude what?

choices.A: Civilization can develop independently in different parts of the world
choices.C: Farming was useless in the Americas
choices.D: All cities must be near the Nile

questions.explanation: It shows civilization can develop independently in different parts of the world.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT something farming made possible for early American peoples?
questions.explanation: Farming did not let people travel instantly between continents; it allowed settling, surplus, and larger communities.

questions.question: After people settled and farmed, surplus food allowed populations to do what?
questions.explanation: Surplus food allowed populations to grow larger over time.

questions.question: Which best explains why maize is called the 'key crop' of the Americas?

choices.A: It was used only for decoration
choices.B: It was the main food that supported growing communities

questions.explanation: Maize was the main food that supported growing communities.

questions.question: Put these stages in the correct order from earliest to latest.

choices.A: Large cities, then learning to farm, then settling
choices.B: Learning to farm, then building villages, then building cities
choices.C: Building cities, then settling, then farming
choices.D: Settling, then large empires, then farming

questions.explanation: The order was learning to farm, then villages, then cities.

questions.question: Which sentence is an EXAMPLE of a turning point caused by farming?

choices.A: People wandered the same way they always had
choices.C: People settled down and built the first villages and cities
choices.D: People forgot how to grow crops

questions.explanation: Settling down and building villages and cities is the turning point farming caused.

questions.question: Which statement about the Three Sisters is TRUE?

choices.A: They were corn, beans, and squash grown together
choices.C: They were three rivers in Asia
choices.D: They were the only crops grown in Egypt

questions.explanation: The Three Sisters were corn, beans, and squash grown together.

questions.question: How were the American civilizations and the river civilizations of Africa and Asia ALIKE?

choices.A: Both were taught by the Romans
choices.C: Both developed farming, cities, and government

questions.explanation: Both developed farming, cities, and government on their own.

questions.question: What was the first big step that allowed permanent communities in the Americas?

choices.D: Learning to farm crops like maize

questions.explanation: Learning to farm crops like maize was the first big step.

questions.question: If American peoples had NEVER learned to farm, what would most likely have happened?

choices.A: They would have built giant cities anyway
choices.B: It would have been much harder to settle down and form large communities
choices.C: They would have invented writing instantly
choices.D: Nothing would have changed at all

questions.explanation: Without farming it would have been much harder to settle down and form large communities.

questions.question: Which of these is the BEST definition of farming?

choices.A: Growing crops and raising food on purpose
choices.C: Moving from place to place searching for food

questions.explanation: Farming means growing crops and raising food on purpose.

questions.question: Which region was NOT settled by the early peoples of the Americas?
questions.explanation: They settled North, Central, and South America, not Northern Europe.

questions.question: Which conclusion is BEST supported by the rise of farming and cities in the Americas?

choices.A: People in faraway places can solve the same problems on their own
choices.B: Only people near rivers can ever build cities
choices.C: Farming was invented only once in history
choices.D: Maize could not feed large groups

questions.explanation: It shows people in faraway places can solve the same problems on their own.

11-2.title: The Maya and Other Civilizations
11-2.learn:
KEY IDEAS — THE MAYA AND AMERICAN CIVILIZATIONS

The MAYA were a great civilization of CENTRAL AMERICA (Mesoamerica), living in the rainforests of what are now Mexico and Central America. Even in the thick jungle, the Maya built impressive stone PYRAMIDS, temples, and large cities with plazas and ball courts.

The Maya were skilled in several areas. They were excellent at ASTRONOMY, carefully studying the sun, moon, and stars. They were strong in MATHEMATICS — remarkably, they understood the idea of ZERO, just as Gupta India did, and used it in their number system. Using their sky knowledge and math, they created a very accurate CALENDAR. The Maya also developed a written LANGUAGE made of symbols called glyphs, which they carved on monuments.

Comparing the Maya to the river civilizations of Africa and Asia shows something important: people in completely SEPARATE parts of the world independently developed the same key features of civilization — CITIES, WRITING, math, calendars, and GOVERNMENT. The Maya prove that complex civilization arose in the Americas on its own. Remember: Maya = Central America, pyramids, astronomy, zero, and an accurate calendar.

questions.question: Where did the Maya civilization develop?
questions.explanation: The Maya lived in Central America.

questions.question: What impressive structures did the Maya build in the rainforest?
questions.explanation: The Maya built stone pyramids and temples.

questions.question: In which subjects were the Maya especially skilled?
questions.explanation: The Maya excelled in astronomy and math.

questions.question: Which important math idea did the Maya understand?
questions.explanation: The Maya understood the concept of zero.

questions.question: The Maya used their knowledge of the sky to create an accurate what?
questions.explanation: The Maya created an accurate calendar.

questions.question: The Maya wrote using a system of what?
questions.explanation: The Maya wrote with symbols called glyphs.

questions.question: What does comparing the Maya to river civilizations show us?

choices.A: Separate peoples independently developed cities, writing, and government

questions.explanation: The Maya independently developed the same key features as river civilizations.

questions.question: Which TWO civilizations both understood the idea of zero?
questions.explanation: Both the Maya and Gupta India understood zero independently.

questions.question: The Maya built large cities even in what kind of environment?

choices.D: A sandy desert with no plants

questions.explanation: The Maya built cities in the rainforest jungle.

questions.question: Which statement BEST describes the Maya?

choices.A: A Central American civilization skilled in astronomy, math, and writing
choices.B: A river civilization in the Middle East
choices.C: Sea traders who created the alphabet

questions.explanation: The Maya were a Central American civilization skilled in astronomy, math, and writing.

questions.question: What is another name for the region of Central America where the Maya lived?
questions.explanation: Central America where the Maya lived is also called Mesoamerica.

questions.question: What did the Maya call the symbols they used for writing?
questions.explanation: The Maya wrote with symbols called glyphs.

questions.question: The Maya studied the sun, moon, and stars. This is the science of what?
questions.explanation: Studying the sun, moon, and stars is astronomy.

questions.question: How did the Maya use their knowledge of astronomy and math together?

choices.B: To create a very accurate calendar

questions.explanation: They combined astronomy and math to create a very accurate calendar.

questions.question: Why was the Maya understanding of zero remarkable?

choices.B: It was the same as Roman numerals
choices.C: It was a difficult math idea they developed on their own

questions.explanation: Zero was a difficult math idea the Maya developed on their own.

questions.question: Which of these did the Maya NOT build?
questions.explanation: The Maya built pyramids, temples, and ball courts, not iron warships.

questions.question: In which two subjects were the Maya especially strong?
questions.explanation: The Maya were especially strong in astronomy and mathematics.

questions.question: Where did the Maya carve their glyph writing?
questions.explanation: The Maya carved glyphs on stone monuments.

questions.question: Which idea did the Maya and Gupta India BOTH develop independently?
questions.explanation: Both the Maya and Gupta India developed the number zero independently.

questions.question: What does the word 'glyph' mean as the Maya used it?
questions.explanation: A glyph is a written symbol.

questions.question: The Maya building cities in a thick jungle shows what about them?

choices.A: They could only live in deserts
choices.B: They were skilled builders who overcame a hard environment

questions.explanation: It shows they were skilled builders who overcame a hard environment.

questions.question: Which list shows key achievements of the Maya?

choices.A: The alphabet, sea trade, and coins
choices.B: Iron tools, the wheel, and gunpowder
choices.D: Pyramids, astronomy, zero, and an accurate calendar

questions.explanation: Maya achievements include pyramids, astronomy, zero, and an accurate calendar.

questions.question: What did the Maya carefully study to gain their sky knowledge?
questions.explanation: They studied the sun, moon, and stars.

questions.question: Which BEST shows that the Maya developed civilization on their own?

choices.B: They created cities, writing, and math without contact with Africa or Asia
choices.D: They had no government at all

questions.explanation: They created cities, writing, and math without contact with Africa or Asia.

questions.question: Today the Maya region is part of which modern nations?
questions.explanation: The Maya lived in what are now Mexico and Central America.

questions.question: Which feature did the Maya share with the river civilizations of Africa and Asia?
questions.explanation: Like the river civilizations, the Maya had a system of writing.

questions.question: What was inside many large Maya cities besides pyramids and temples?
questions.explanation: Maya cities had plazas and ball courts.

questions.question: Which statement about the Maya is NOT true?

choices.B: They understood the idea of zero

questions.explanation: The Maya did not live in northern Europe; they lived in Central America.

questions.question: Why is an accurate calendar useful to a farming civilization like the Maya?

choices.A: It lets them fly to the moon
choices.B: It replaces the need for food
choices.C: It is used only for decoration
choices.D: It helps them know the seasons and when to plant

questions.explanation: An accurate calendar helps farmers know the seasons and when to plant.

questions.question: The Maya number system was notable because it included what?
questions.explanation: The Maya number system included the number zero.

questions.question: How were the Maya and Gupta India ALIKE?

choices.A: Both were river civilizations in Egypt
choices.B: Both understood and used the idea of zero

questions.explanation: Both the Maya and Gupta India understood and used the idea of zero.

questions.question: Which is the BEST description of Maya glyphs?

choices.C: Symbols that made up a written language

questions.explanation: Glyphs were symbols that made up a written language.

questions.question: What does the Maya civilization prove about the Americas?

choices.D: Complex civilization arose there on its own

questions.explanation: The Maya prove complex civilization arose in the Americas on its own.

questions.question: Which of these is an EXAMPLE of Maya skill in astronomy?

choices.C: Carefully tracking the movements of the sun, moon, and stars

questions.explanation: Tracking the movements of the sun, moon, and stars shows their astronomy skill.

questions.question: Put these Maya achievements in order from gathering knowledge to using it.

choices.A: Create a calendar, then study the stars, then learn math
choices.B: Study the stars and learn math, then create an accurate calendar
choices.C: Build pyramids, then forget astronomy, then study stars
choices.D: Invent the wheel, then study the stars, then build temples

questions.explanation: They studied the stars and learned math, then used that to create an accurate calendar.

questions.question: Which civilization built stone pyramids in the rainforests of Central America?
questions.explanation: The Maya built stone pyramids in the rainforests of Central America.

questions.question: Which feature of civilization did the Maya develop, just as river civilizations did?
questions.explanation: Like river civilizations, the Maya developed government to organize their cities.

questions.question: What is the BEST meaning of the word 'calendar' as the Maya used it?

choices.A: A system for tracking days, months, and seasons

questions.explanation: A calendar is a system for tracking days, months, and seasons.

questions.question: Which big idea do the Maya help prove about world history?

choices.A: Separate peoples can independently develop the same features of civilization
choices.C: Writing was invented only in Egypt

questions.explanation: They show separate peoples can independently develop the same features of civilization.

questions.question: Which statement BEST summarizes the Maya civilization?

choices.A: A Central American people known for pyramids, astronomy, zero, and an accurate calendar
choices.B: A desert people who only herded animals
choices.C: A European empire that conquered Rome
choices.D: A group that never built cities or writing

questions.explanation: The Maya were a Central American people known for pyramids, astronomy, zero, and an accurate calendar.
